subject: RTO/RPO evidence and restore walkthrough — FinCorp assessment
messages:
From: Natalie Ortiz <natalie.ortiz@fincorp-audit.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: FinCorp Compliance <compliance@fincorp.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: RTO/RPO evidence and restore walkthrough — FinCorp assessment

Hi Markus,

We’re performing the FinCorp infrastructure assessment for Q4 and need to collect artifacts demonstrating your disaster recovery posture for the hosted API service. Specifically, could you provide the following by next Wednesday (11/11):

- The current service restore runbook (versioned) used by ops for full-region recovery.
- Logs or play-by-play for the most recent restoration exercises (restore execution logs) including timestamps for start/finish.
- RTO and RPO measurement summaries and the methodology used to calculate them (raw measurement file preferred).
- Point-of-contact for on-call/ops who can run a short remote walkthrough (20–30 min) with our team.

We’ll also need a short statement confirming that the artifacts reflect production processes used during the last exercised failover. If you have a hosted Drive folder or ticket we can reference, that would help speed validation.

Thanks,
Natalie Ortiz
Senior Auditor, FinCorp Assessments
Natalie Ortiz
FinCorp Audit Services

---
Note: We will treat attachments as confidential.

Action items:
- Can you confirm which runbook version is authoritative and attach the PDF?
- Export the most recent restore execution log (prefer human-readable timestamps) and the measurement CSV; include how RTO/RPO were calculated.
- Provide a single ops contact (name, title, phone, and preferred windows next week).
- I'll consolidate and send the response to Natalie.

Please attach artifacts directly in your reply or drop them in the Drive folder (link to follow). If there are controls or caveats we should call out (partial failover, manual steps), flag them explicitly so I can set expectations with the audit team.

-Markus

Markus,

We’ve pulled the requested artifacts and created a short packet. Attached here:

- redwood_runbook_service-restore_v2.pdf (authoritative runbook; last updated 2026-09-28)
- restore-execution-20261015.log (full restore run, timestamps include operator actions)
- rto-rpo-measurements-2026Q3.csv (raw measurement samples used for the summary)
- ops-contact-list-2026.csv (on-call rotation and escalation contacts)

Notes / clarifications:
- RTO measurement method: measured from incident declaration to service-level verification (synthetic checks + sample request validation). The summary in the CSV includes both automated probe timestamps and manual verification markers.
- RPO: asynchronous replication with max observed delta ~ 12 minutes in the October exercise; we capture replication lag at 1-minute granularity in the CSV.
- The October exercise was a simulated primary-region restore using the documented runbook. Several manual steps (DNS TTL decreases, cross-region load balancer reconfiguration) are expected and listed in the runbook.

I also created a JIRA ticket for tracking evidence submission: SUP-1123. I can be the POC for the walkthrough — available next week Tue–Thu 09:00–12:00 PT. If you’d prefer someone from SRE engineering who led the run, Priyom is available afternoons.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_service-restore_v2.pdf (PDF), restore-execution-20261015.log (text), rto-rpo-measurements-2026Q3.csv (CSV), ops-contact-list-2026.csv (CSV)

-Irene

Hi Natalie,

Thanks for the clear ask. Please find the requested artifacts attached and summarized below. We’ve also shared a Drive folder and opened JIRA SUP-1123 for traceability.

Quick summary (for your reviewer):
- Authoritative runbook: redwood_runbook_service-restore_v2.pdf (attached). Last update: 2026-09-28.
- Recent restoration exercise: restore-execution-20261015.log (attached). Total measured restore wall-clock: 3 hours 52 minutes (start to verification).
- RTO/RPO raw data: rto-rpo-measurements-2026Q3.csv (attached). RTO methodology: incident declaration -> execution -> synthetic verification. Calculated production RTO target: 4 hours.
- RPO: asynchronous replication; observed max lag in October exercise: 12 minutes. We use 1-minute sampling to capture lag.
- Ops POC for walkthrough: Irene Choi, Director Production Operations (irene_choi@redwoodinference.com), available Tue–Thu 09:00–12:00 PT. Alternative: Priyom Das (SRE lead) afternoons.

Drive folder (evidence): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cDefGHqRestoreEvidence
JIRA: SUP-1123
HubSpot reference: HS-4572

Caveats / controls to note:
- Certain DNS and external-provider changes used during the run require manual confirmation; these are called out in the runbook with operator checklists.
- The October exercise used a seeded dataset and synthetic probes; production variability is noted in the CSV and the runbook.

Attachments included: redwood_runbook_service-restore_v2.pdf, restore-execution-20261015.log, rto-rpo-measurements-2026Q3.csv, ops-contact-list-2026.csv

If you’d like, we can do a 20–30 minute remote walkthrough next week. Irene is available in the mornings PT — let me know a couple of times that work for FinCorp and we’ll confirm.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Reliability
